Terms click to expand diagram & trace

▶
Own spend vs spend including delegated work — Own spend is an agent's own inferences; including delegated work adds those of every agent it delegated to.
 
invoke_agent Catalog
├── chat gemini-2.5-flash         900  # own
└── transfer → Checkout
invoke_agent Checkout
├── chat gemini-2.5-flash       1,000  # delegated
└── invoke_agent Reconciler
    └── chat gemini-2.5-flash-lite 700 # delegated
# Catalog incl. delegated = 2,600
▶
Call vs transfer — In a call the caller waits and the callee's span nests; in a transfer (pass_control) the source stops and the target's span may be a sibling.
 
# call (nested)
invoke_agent Storefront
└── invoke_agent Catalog
    └── invoke_agent Checkout
        # lineage: {Storefront, Catalog, Checkout}

# transfer with pass_control (sibling)
invoke_agent Storefront
├── invoke_agent Catalog   # ends at transfer
└── invoke_agent Checkout
    # lineage: {Storefront, Catalog, Checkout}
▶
Re-entry — An agent runs again inside its own invocation, e.g. a sub-agent transfers back to it.
 
invoke_agent Storefront
│ # lineage: {Storefront}
└── invoke_agent Checkout
    │ # lineage: {Storefront, Checkout}
    └── invoke_agent Storefront
        # lineage: {Storefront, Checkout}
        # already in set: no duplicate
▶
Delegation lineage — The set of agents on the way to the current agent, propagated with the request.
 
invoke_agent Storefront
│ {Storefront}
├── invoke_agent Catalog
│   {Storefront, Catalog}
└── invoke_agent Checkout
    │ {Storefront, Catalog, Checkout}
    └── invoke_agent Reconciler
        {Storefront, Catalog, Checkout, Reconciler}
▶
Roll-up — Each inference adds one .rollup point per agent in its lineage.
 
# Reconciler's chat (700 input tokens)
gen_ai.client.inference.usage.input_tokens
  += 700 {gen_ai.agent.name="Reconciler", …}
gen_ai.client.inference.usage.rollup.input_tokens  += 700 {gen_ai.agent.name="Storefront", …}gen_ai.client.inference.usage.rollup.input_tokens  += 700 {gen_ai.agent.name="Catalog", …}gen_ai.client.inference.usage.rollup.input_tokens  += 700 {gen_ai.agent.name="Checkout", …}gen_ai.client.inference.usage.rollup.input_tokens  += 700 {gen_ai.agent.name="Reconciler", …}
▶
Summable — Summing across the attribute counts each token once; the roll-up's gen_ai.agent.name is not.
 
# pin one agent: counts each token once
sum(...rollup.input_tokens
  {gen_ai.agent.name="Catalog"})   # → 700   ✓

# sum across all agents: 4x for depth 4
sum(...rollup.input_tokens)        # → 2,800 ✗

Motivation: attributing token spend to agents

Flow diagram · Scenario 1

Trace · same flow (input tokens)

invoke_agent Storefront
├── chat gemini-2.5-pro            1,200  # route
├── invoke_agent Catalog
│   ├── chat gemini-2.5-flash        900
│   └── transfer → Checkout               # pass_control
├── invoke_agent Checkout
│   ├── chat gemini-2.5-flash      1,000
│   └── invoke_agent Reconciler
│       └── chat gemini-2.5-flash-lite 700
└── chat gemini-2.5-pro            1,500  # final

What the leading approach can't answer today:

✗ A lead agent's spend including delegated work

For Catalog it shows 900 of 2,600 — nothing delegated below the main agent can be priced by model.

✗ Spend that follows delegation, not ownership

StockLedger is owned by Catalog. When it works for Reconciler, its spend belongs to Reconciler.

"Main agent" depends on the layer you look from

Our Storefront example assumes one root name fits everyone. Depending on the layer, different people call a different thing "the agent" — and mean something different by "main":

1 · Runtime SRE — sees the deployed server job 
client.agent_engines.create(..., config={"display_name": "prime-checker-prod"})
2 · Protocol (A2A) TL — sees the A2A service their team maintains 
agent_card = create_agent_card(agent_name="ADK Prime Agent", ...)
3 · Framework SWE — sees the root object written for the task 
root_agent = Agent(name="root_agent", tools=[AgentTool(prime_agent)])

One main_agent slot: one view squats it

gen_ai.main_agent.name = ???  # privileges one:
  "prime-checker-prod"   # SRE's server job
  "ADK Prime Agent"      # TL's A2A service
  "root_agent"           # SWE's root object

With lineage: all three MAY join — no "main" slot

gen_ai.agent.lineage = {
  "prime-checker-prod",  # SRE · runtime
  "ADK Prime Agent",     # TL  · A2A card
  "root_agent",          # SWE · framework
  "prime_agent",         # sub-agent
}

Taking a stance on what "main" means privileges one viewpoint and locks out the other two. Because lineage is just a set with no privileged main_agent role, every layer may add its name and each role queries .rollup by the one it works with.

Proposal

1. Propagate the delegation lineage

The lineage grows with each hop

invoke Storefront
Storefront
call Catalog
StorefrontCatalog
transfer → Checkout
StorefrontCatalogCheckout
call Reconciler
StorefrontCatalogCheckoutReconciler

Dark chip = current agent, which gets the own-spend data point.

# call, or transfer with gen_ai.transfer.mode = return_to_caller
callee.lineage = caller.lineage | {callee}

# transfer with gen_ai.transfer.mode = pass_control
# (OpenAI Agents SDK handoffs, ADK transfer_to_agent)
target.lineage = source.lineage | {target}   # even after the source ended

# re-entry: set semantics, no duplicates
{"Storefront", "Checkout"} | {"Storefront"} == {"Storefront", "Checkout"}

# boundary wrappers (runtime, A2A card, framework root) MAY each add their name
lineage |= {runtime_name, card_name, framework_root_name}

Diagrams: call vs transfer, re-entry.

in process: OTel Context across processes: mechanism TBD back to caller: nothing

2. Metrics: one attribute added, one roll-up added

# existing inference counters: gain one attribute       … = existing attributes
  gen_ai.client.inference.usage.input_tokens               {…, + gen_ai.agent.name}
  gen_ai.client.inference.usage.output_tokens              {…, + gen_ai.agent.name}
  gen_ai.client.inference.usage.cache_read.input_tokens    {…, + gen_ai.agent.name}
  gen_ai.client.inference.usage.cache_write.input_tokens   {…, + gen_ai.agent.name}
  gen_ai.client.inference.usage.reasoning.output_tokens    {…, + gen_ai.agent.name}

# new: one point per inference per agent in its lineage
+ gen_ai.client.inference.usage.rollup.input_tokens        {…, gen_ai.agent.name}+ gen_ai.client.inference.usage.rollup.output_tokens       {…, gen_ai.agent.name}

Queries, with results from the example

# own spend of Catalog
sum(gen_ai.client.inference.usage.input_tokens{
  gen_ai.agent.name="Catalog"})                                 # → 900

# Catalog including delegated work
sum(gen_ai.client.inference.usage.rollup.input_tokens{
  gen_ai.agent.name="Catalog"})                                 # → 2,600

# Storefront end to end (it only ever runs as the main agent)
sum(gen_ai.client.inference.usage.rollup.input_tokens{
  gen_ai.agent.name="Storefront"})                              # → 5,300

# price it: Catalog including delegated work, by model
sum by (gen_ai.response.model)(
  gen_ai.client.inference.usage.rollup.input_tokens{
    gen_ai.agent.name="Catalog"})
#   → gemini-2.5-flash 1,900 · gemini-2.5-flash-lite 700

Summable across the attribute?

agent.nameoperation.nameprovider.namerequest.modelresponse.modelserver.*token.modality
inference.usage.* ✓✓✓✓✓✓✓
inference.usage.rollup.* ✗✓✓✓✓✓✓

The points written for one inference differ only in gen_ai.agent.name (and gen_ai.token.modality, whose parts add up), so only the agent column can double count: summing the roll-up across agents counts a token once per agent in its lineage. Generator check: 40 inference and 90 roll-up points across six traces.

Leading puts main_agent.name on the existing counters, so they grow with sharing. The proposal keeps them at one agent per series and pays only on the new roll-up, which is keyed by one agent and never multiplied by main agents.

A × K = one series per (agent, model) pair. A × M × K = one per (agent, main agent, model).

Series per counter; other attributes multiply both sides equally. Lower: each agent under one main agent. Upper: every agent under every main agent.

Own spend

equal

Both read it from the inference counters by gen_ai.agent.name.

Re-entry

equal

When Storefront runs again inside its own invocation, both give its end-to-end spend as 8,800. diagram

Data points

leading better

Leading: 1 per inference per counter. Proposal: that, plus 1 roll-up point per lineage agent.

Summability

leading better

Every leading-approach metric can be summed over any attribute. The roll-up can't be summed across agents.

Context size

leading better

Leading: two names (main agent, current agent). Proposal: a set that grows with delegation depth, plus the current agent.

4. What recorders must uphold

One recorder

Whoever records the inference counters also records the roll-up, reading the lineage from context as it reads gen_ai.agent.name.

No duplicates

At most 1 roll-up point per inference per agent.

No gaps

Every hop propagates the lineage. A gap undercounts the agents above it.

Unique names

Across all services sharing a lineage, e.g. shop/Catalog.

Trusted input

Accept an incoming lineage only from trusted callers.

Alternatives considered

A

agent.name + main_agent.name on inference counters

The leading approach, shown in the left column of the summary. The proposal keeps its gen_ai.agent.name half.

✓ always summable ✓ main vs sub-agent runs separated ✗ incl. delegated below the main agent ✗ series grow with shared agents
B

invoke_agent own and total token histograms

Each invoke_agent records its own tokens and its subtree's. Main agent totals from top-level records are correct. Totals of nested invocations follow the span tree, not the delegation. Input tokens:

CaseAgentB reportsWith lineage
transfer as sibling spanCatalog9002,600
re-entry by nested transfersCheckout13,5007,600
✓ tokens per request (p50 / p95) ✗ totals mix models: can't price
C

One new metric with a direct | delegated attribute

sum(gen_ai.agent.usage.input_tokens)                                 # → 10,300  ✗
sum(gen_ai.agent.usage.input_tokens{gen_ai.usage.attribution="direct"}) # → 5,300   ✓

Forgetting the filter inflates own spend by the token-weighted mean lineage length (1.7–2.9× in the six traces). The roll-up has the same trap across agents. The difference is that own spend stays on a fully summable metric, as the OTel rule of thumb asks: aggregations over all attributes SHOULD be meaningful.
